findings.problem: Case (a) calls markAbandonedPending(db, -60_000), which computes a cutoff 60s in the future and therefore sweeps EVERY currently-pending row in the shared PGlite instance for the whole file (including the never-cleaned-up 'Pending Role' row left behind by the listByUser test at line ~360), not just the row under test. The aggregate assertion expect(swept).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1) tolerates this, and the test's real assertions are scoped to the specific row id, so this is not a false-green today, but it is a broad, undocumented-scope side effect on shared DB state that could bite a future test appended after this describe block (a new test relying on a lingering pending row would be silently swept).
findings.fix: Either scope the sweep-simulation to the row under test (e.g. back-date created_at for this one row like the existing TTL tests do, instead of a future global cutoff), or keep this describe block last in the file (as it is today) and add a one-line comment noting the intentional file-wide sweep side effect so a future test author does not get surprised.
